title: A worker verification's test shards run on ready hosts while a merge trial starts
description: A worker's host-run test check over a large test list, with two ready compute hosts reached through graphyard-host-shim under a strict heavy-job cap of one. Its shards run on both hosts as a merge trial's do, and it holds no heavy-job slot while they run there, so a merge trial takes the one slot at once. Master status's remoteShards shows the worker verification as the latest run, with every shard run remotely and both hosts ready. A one-script check beside a declared Postgres Compose service runs whole on a ready host, which starts the service, runs the script on its network and removes the project, else on this machine when no host is ready or the host drops it; the reason shows beside the host's load line in master status and on Workers. One command, host add YOU@HOST in a terminal, prepares a host over SSH and adds it; a second coordinator joins it by host share, no root, and runs shards there. One host serves two installs: each install's key reaches its own release's helper, and removing one install's key leaves the other working. The loop sends this release's helper to a host on another one, and the host takes it only when its digest matches; its shards then go there, and one whose update fails reads away with the reason. A ready host on an older helper from before the update verb stays ready, and master status adds one line: HOST runs an older helper: run mainworks host add YOU@HOST in a terminal to update it. A host without Docker reads away saying whether its unit is disabled or failed. The warm image, keyed to main's commit and lockfile, reaches ready hosts first, starts the CLI under 0.6 CPU-seconds and rebuilds a head's changed source. While a leftover limit file fixes the budget and a host is ready, master status names it and hostHeavyJobs=auto, which removes it. A host takes test shards while its busy cores plus the shards placed there stay under its cores less two; master status shows each host's shards beside its busy cores. A host on the run-shard:2 helper and one on run-shard:3 each take shards in the form they accept, a host that refuses reads away with the refusal, and the warm image links Postgres's native libraries so its tests start there.

steps.name: Add a fake host with one command that prepares it over SSH, then let a second coordinator join it by share and run a shard there
Run a worker verification on two fake hosts and start a merge trial beside it
Place shards on hosts by free cores, show each host's shards in master status and raise one line while this machine is overloaded beside a half-free host
Show a leftover limit file in master status while hosts are ready, and lift it with hostHeavyJobs=auto
Run a script check and its Postgres service whole on a fake host, and on this machine when the host is away, with the reason in master status and on the Workers page
Run a declared check with a service image built locally on the coordinator (never pushed) and verify it is sent once and answers on the compute host
Read a fake host whose Docker unit is not enabled and one whose unit failed, and show the reason
Prepare one fake host for two installs at different helper releases, probe each through its own helper, and name the older helper in one master status line
Update a fake host's older helper from the loop, send it shards, and refuse a helper with the wrong digest
Build the commit- and lockfile-keyed warm image, verify warm CLI startup under 0.6 CPU-seconds and head source rebuild on a remote host
Run trial shards on a run-shard:2 helper and a run-shard:3 helper, mark a refusing helper away with its refusal, and link Postgres's libraries in the warm image
